overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford Social Service Coordinator Jason Stone to discuss the diverse resources available through the City's Health Department. The meeting covered the functions of the Office of Prevention and Outreach, mental health trends, and methods for residents to access social and housing support.

items.title: Professional Background of Jason Stone
items.summary: Social Service Coordinator Jason Stone discussed his professional transition from substance use disorder and community corrections fields to municipal service in Medford.

items.title: Medford Health Department Core Responsibilities
items.summary: Stone identified the department's primary functions as inspectional services, environmental health, public health nursing, and animal control.

items.title: Office of Prevention and Outreach (OPO)
items.summary: The discussion highlighted the OPO's role in health equity, grant management, and its unique structure involving recovery coaches and community liaisons.

items.title: Coordination and Triage of Social Services
items.summary: Stone described his role as a resource connector who triages calls to assist residents with navigating complex housing, healthcare, and financial assistance applications.

items.title: Analysis of Mental Health Trends
items.summary: The speakers discussed the rising demand for mental health services, attributing the surge to increased awareness, reduced stigma, and the long-term impacts of the pandemic.

items.title: Medford Connects and Prevention Programming
items.summary: Stone explained how language-specific community liaisons and school-based prevention coordinators work to engage underserved populations and provide early intervention.

items.title: Emergency Response and Police Collaboration
items.summary: The guest detailed the coordination between social services and the Medford Police Department's embedded mental health clinicians for crisis response and 911 triage.

items.title: Systemic Challenges and Housing Shortages
items.summary: Stone identified the lack of affordable, short-term housing and general nonprofit staffing shortages as the most significant hurdles in the social service sector.

items.title: Community Access and Contact Information
items.summary: The meeting concluded with Stone sharing contact details and announcing weekly open office hours held every Wednesday at the Medford Public Library.

subject: Medford Health Department Social Service Resources
